articles.content:
As NBC marks its 100th anniversary this year, another mainstay of the media landscape is turning 80: book publisher Farrar, Straus & Giroux.

The literary division of Macmillan Publishers has grown from a small boutique into a home for Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and National Book Award recipients. On Monday night, as NBCUniversal CEO Mike Cavanagh hosted a star-studded centennial party at the Rainbow Room atop 30 Rockefeller Plaza, FSG President and Publisher Mitzi Angel presided over her own bash.

The celebration, held at the historic event venue Storied in Chelsea, drew its own share of distinguished guests. While late-night host Jimmy Fallon was among the A-listers at NBC, his Tonight Show drummer, Roots frontman Ahmir “Questlove” Thompson, made a surprise appearance at the FSG gathering, delivering a DJ set. Angel addressed the crowd in attendance to salute the company's durability and make an impassioned case for its mission during a time of cultural transformation.

“We live in an age of algorithms, and algorithms are very good at what can be measured now. Literature works on another timescale, in a place measurement can’t reach. A machine can now produce the most probable next sentence. Our job is to find, and to keep, the improbable one: the distinctive, idiosyncratic voice with a music of its own,” she said.

Reflecting on the milestone, she added, “Eighty years is a long time in publishing, but not so long in the history of literature. A publishing house, finally, is people standing behind books, for as long as it takes.”

articles.content:
Kristin Hannah’s best-selling historical fiction book The Nightingale will be made into a movie after all.

The project was first sparked before the COVID-19 pandemic, which slowed momentum on the making of the film. Now the movie has a theatrical release date set and a growing cast attached to the story.

For everything we know about The Nightingale movie, read on.

When will The Nightingale movie come out?

TriStar first set February 12, 2027 as the release date for the film, but then the adaptation was pushed to March 19 so that it has Easter weekend (March 28) to capitalize on. Is there a trailer for The Nightingale movie?

Yes, a trailer arrived Nov. 19 giving a glimpse of what the Fanning sisters' French characters will go through in the film .

Who will be in The Nightingale movie?

Sisters Dakota and Elle Fanning , who have been attached to star and produce since the adaptation started gaining traction in 2019, will portray sisters Vianne and Isabelle.

Deadline exclusively reported that Edmund Donovan ( Late Fame ) landed a starring role alongside the sisters in January 2026. Details of his role are under wraps.

Next to join as first reported by Deadline are Mark Rylance  ( The BFG, Ready Player One ) and  Shira Haas ( Unorthodox, Captain America: Brave New World ).

Deadline broke the news of a quartet of castings that round out the film's ensemble: Albrecht Schuch , Douglas Hodge, Gwilym Lee and Vinette Robinson.

What is Kristin Hannah’s The Nightingale about?

The story centers sisters Vianne Mauriac and Isabelle Rossignol, who experience German-occupied France during World War II in their own ways. Vianne, the older sister, is more cautious while Isabelle boasts a rebellious spirit. The sisters split up during the war, "resisting in different ways" as Fanning put it when she did Deadline's Take Ten interview series . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Who else is behind The Nightingale movie?

Michael Morris is directing the film. Dana Stevens ( The Woman King ) wrote the script for the film. Elizabeth Cantillon will produce for The Cantillon Company, alongside the Fannings and Brittany Kahan Ward for the Fanning sisters' production company Lewellen Pictures, and Reese Witherspoon and Lauren Neustadter for Hello Sunshine. The Nightingale was the Reese’s Book Club selection for March 2023. Nicole Brown and Shary Shirazi are overseeing for TriStar Pictures.

TriStar first acquired the film rights in 2015 with Ann Peacock attached to write. Writer-director Michelle MacLaren and co-writer John Sayles were involved in a later iteration, with the Fannings initially boarding to star in a version helmed by Mélanie Laurent from Stevens’ script . At first, the film was set to hit theaters Christmas Day of 2020, and then it shifted a few more times landing on Dec. 22, 2022 , but when the Covid pandemic kept delaying the making of the movie, Laurent stepped back to attend to other projects.

Has The Nightingale started production?

Yes, Kristin Hannah posted at the end of March that the film had started production. Elle Fanning did press for Margo's Got Money Troubles in April before the show's premiere on Apple TV, but she had hinted as had her sister Dakota, that they would start shooting in a few weeks when Deadline spoke with them at SXSW Film Festival 2026.

Deadline also interviewed Lauren Neustadter , President of Film and Television at Reese Witherspoon's Production Company Hello Sunshine while she was on set in Budapest, where the film is shooting.

articles.title: IDFA Awards Ceremony: ‘The Year Of The Ghost’ And ‘Memories Of Lightning’ Earn Top Prizes

articles.content:
Director Louis HotHotHot is living up to his name. His feature documentary The Year of the Ghost won Best Film in International Competition Thursday as the 39th International Documentary Festival Amsterdam presented its awards.

The Chinese-born filmmaker, also known as Louis Liu, also won Best Editing in International Competition, sharing that prize with his co-editor Chris van Oers.

The IDFA program says in The Year of the Ghost , HotHotHot “fearlessly turns his camera on his own family… Using archival footage, animation, and unflinchingly candid conversations, Louis HotHotHot explores how modern Chinese history and misogyny affect the lives of women. This intimate family portrait unfolds into a compelling story about the status of women and changing family culture in China.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Documentary IDFA Announces Winning Projects In Forum Section, With Prizes Worth More Than €30,000 Documentary 'NAZA' Team Sticking To Plan To Release Shattering Documentary On The Guardian Website Within Weeks -- IDFA

“The jury was astonished by this work of singular artistic vision exploring deep family dynamics and connections, set against the wider societal forces and gender constraints inherited across generations,” wrote jury members Barbara Orlicz-Szczypuła, Hania Mroué, Katy Léna N'diaye, Oscar winner Laura Poitras, and Luuk Bouwman. “Told with bold honesty, a rare attention to detail, cinematic curiosity, and love.”

Separately, The Year of the Ghost won Best Dutch Film, earning a €5,000 prize.

The Special Mention for International Competition went to Hazara Town by Khadim Dai. Scroll for the full list of awards.

The IDFA Award for Best Directing (worth €5,000) in the International Competition went to Joël Richmond Mathieu Akafou for Lonan Tché .

The jury wrote, “Through its deeply attaching characters and the subtitle proximity the filmmaker established with them, the film depicts two overgrown kids in their quest for a dream they might never reach, elevating them to almost mythical figures, enduring their human condition.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Best Cinematography in the International Competition went to Bardi by Tala Hadid, with cinematography by Tala Hadid.

In the Envision Competition, which IDFA considers to be of equal importance to International Competition, Best Film was awarded to Riccardo Giacconi for Memories of Lightning . That award also comes with a €15,000 cash prize.

In the feature documentary, “Thirty-year old freelance radio journalist Sibilla travels to a village in Le Marche, central Italy. She plans to make an audio documentary about a shocking event that took place there in 1982, but the village is now little more than a ghost town – earthquakes and an artificial lake have destroyed much of it,” reads the IDFA program description. “Still, she tries to capture memories to create a soundscape of the past with her microphone.”

Jury members for the Envision Competition included Firouzeh Khosrovani, Hélder Beja, Hicham Khalidi, Isabel Pagliai, and Jonathan Perel. They wrote, “A studio, a village, a hill. A device that renders irrelevant the distinction between what is real and unreal, that exercises precise control over what is said and what is left unsaid, that stretches time and hunts down stories. A film that captures the silence of things falling, like distant flashes of lightning that are sure to herald the storm.”

Sibilla Scinti Roger, the protagonist of Memories of Lightning , won the award for Outstanding Artistic Contribution. Best Directing (worth €5,000) in the Envision Competition was awarded to Yuula Benivolski for The Black Box Is Orange .

The Special Mention for Envision Competition went to Memories by Anna Falguères.

all that appears solid is built on blood , directed by Izdihar Afyouni and Gelare Khoshgozaran, won the IDFA Award for Best Short Documentary, which comes with a €5,000 cash prize.

“In a world saturated with images of violence, this short film interrogates what images can hold when representation becomes impossible,” said the jury, comprised of Ana Bravo-Pérez, Diana Toucedo, and Yaser Kassab. “Through abstraction, fragmentation, grain, texture, and the material transformation of the film image, documented atrocities are displaced from their conventional modes of representation. The image becomes matter: a site of rupture, disturbance and resistance, where memory exceeds the limits of visibility and what can be shown.”

A Special Mention in the IDFA Competition for Short Documentary went to Six Weeks, 3 Days, and All the Years Before by Ankita Gusain.

The IDFA DocLab Award for Immersive Non-Fiction went to Michał Stankiewicz for Being in You . The award is accompanied by a €5,000 cash prize.

“The winner proposes a new way of perceiving the relationship between the protagonist and the viewer: a new immersive point of view in which the digital protagonist and the physical viewer melt together into one,” observed jurors Blake Kammerdiener, Natalie Paneng, and Roel Wouters. “Through a tender exploration of life and death, this project invited us to see how VR can be a tool to memorialize while also bringing a sense of embodied presence.”

The Special Mention for the IDFA DocLab Competition for Immersive Non-Fiction went to Shifting Connections by Tungyen Chou.

Director Ant Hampton won the IDFA DocLab Award for Digital Storytelling with All the Downtime , earning a €5,000 cash prize. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

“Out of visual noise; slowly, you are instructed how to use your fingers to read a performance through a book, synchronizing multiple temporalities,” said jurors Abel Enklaar, Claudix Vanesix, and Pegah Tabassinejad. “This project gently crosses the borders. It exists in between mediums, crafting a slowly escalating waterfall of cinematic moments drifting up from the pages. The work invites us to see the increasing entanglements between technocapitalism, precarious labor conditions, automation of human work, disregards of natural ecosystems, and the new warlords of corporate fascism.”

The Special Mention for the IDFA DocLab Competition for Digital Storytelling went to Plum Road Tea Dream by Samuel Baidoo.

Along with the Special Mention for International Competition, Hazara Town won two awards: Best First Feature, which comes with a €5,000 prize, and the FIPRESCI Award chosen by international film critics (FIPRESCI jurors included Hrvoje Pukšec, Loeke de Waal, and Paola Casella).

The Year of the Ghost and Memories of Lightning are the winners of the top awards at the 38th edition of the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam ( IDFA ), unveiled at a ceremony held at the Dutch city’s Eye Filmmuseum.

The Year of the Ghost from director Louis HotHotHot, a co-production between the Netherlands and China, won the IDFA Award for best film in the international competition section, along with two additional honors.

Like in his debut feature Four Journeys , the filmmaker turned his camera on his own family, prompted by the death of his father. "Due to COVID restrictions, the filmmaker cannot make it to China in time to say goodbye," reads a synopsis. Once reunited with his mother and sister, he films them "as they struggle to find a new way to live." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV CBS Inks New Deal to Air Kennedy Center Honors THR Spotlight It Girl India Amarteifo's Queen's Gambit

"The jury was astonished by this work of singular artistic vision exploring deep family dynamics and connections, set against the wider societal forces and gender constraints inherited across generations," the jury said. "Told with bold honesty, a rare attention to detail, cinematic curiosity and love."

Meanwhile, the IDFA Award for best film in the fest's Envision Competition, along with another honor, went to Riccardo Giacconi for Memories of Lightning , a France-Italy co-production. The film follows radio journalist Sibilla, who travels to a village in central Italy to make an audio documentary about a shocking murder that took place there in 1982, but the village is now little more than a ghost town. "Still, she tries to capture memories to create a soundscape of the past with her microphone," reads a synopsis. "Little by little, the story emerges of a horrific murder that is part of her family history. The victim, a 14-year-old girl, was Sibilla’s aunt."

Said the jury: “A studio, a village, a hill. A device that renders irrelevant the distinction between what is real and unreal, that exercises precise control over what is said and what is left unsaid, that stretches time and hunts down stories. Hazara Town is named after a neighborhood in the Pakistani city of Quetta, which got its name because it is home to so many members of the Hazara ethnic group. What do Disney Parks, Make-A-Wish, and the Hallmark Channel all have in common? They love making dreams come true, and that’s exactly what happened for one teenage Hallmark movie superfan who has dreamt about being in one of the cable channel’s movies for a very long time.

Both Ceci and her mom got to appear in what is apparently one of the major scenes in the holiday romance film, titled Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True . They can be seen as hotel guests, sitting in the lobby of Disney’s Polynesian Village Resort holding Minnie Mouse and Dumbo plushies. I know I’m definitely going to be keeping my eyes open for the mother-daughter duo when the movie premieres as part of the 2026 TV Schedule on the Hallmark Channel on November 28th at 8 p.m. ET.

Filming wrapped early this year on what could be Hallmark’s best Countdown to Christmas movie of 2026, but the magic hasn’t stopped for Ceci, who was surprised once again when her entire family was flown back out to Walt Disney World to attend the red-carpet premiere.

All of this is making me more excited for the film! Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True centers on Lindsey (Chabert), who plans to spend the holidays at Disney World with her extended family. In addition to having the best holiday ever, Lindsey also makes a wish at Cinderella’s Fountain for a love worthy of a fairytale to find her.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The story of Henry Cavill's time as Superman will forever be bittersweet for a lot of DC movie fans. Cavill seemed custom-made for the role of Clark Kent/Superman, but director Zack Snyder's Man of Steel (2012) was seen as a divisive introduction to the character. Even though fans generally accepted (if not enjoyed) Cavill as Superman, Snyder's subsequent film, Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice , made things even more divisive – and that's when things got weird.

After years of debacle getting him into a proper Justice League movie, it looked like Henry Cavill was done with the DC Extended Universe franchise for good. Then Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson gave fans the false hope that Cavill was about to enter a whole new era of being Superman, thanks to the now-infamous post-credits scene of Johnson's DC film, Black Adam . Cavill never suited up as Superman after that, but now you can at least get a behind-the-scenes look at the last time he put on the Superman suit to film his Black Adam cameo.

I saw that #HenryCavill was trending so I thought I'd add my connection to him. I've only ever worked with him once & only for about 3 hours. I only shot 1 scene with him, but it was pretty iconic. Would he make a good #jamesbond007 ? Maybe, but he made a brilliant Man of Steel. pic.twitter.com/34NYOYkSr5

Cinematographer Steven Hall posted a fond memory of when he worked with Henry Cavill on Black Adam . In his post he writes "I saw that #HenryCavill was trending so I thought I'd add my connection to him. I've only ever worked with him once & only for about 3 hours. I only shot 1 scene with him, but it was pretty iconic. Would he make a good #jamesbond007 ? Maybe, but he made a brilliant Man of Steel."

Cavill name is one that regularly goes viral on social media, whether it's fans talking about one of the new projects he's attached to ( Voltron, Highlander, Warhammer 40,000 ) or the never-ending debates about his previous roles as Superman or The Witcher protagonist Geralt of Rivia. He's also spent years being regularly mentioned in discussions about the next James Bond, ever since talk of Daniel Craig's successor began. Now Batman actor Robert Pattinson is the new Bond – casting news that has resonated all across the world. While early signs point to fans overwhelmingly approving of Robert Pattinson as James Bond, Cavill's name has once again been dragged up as a popular alternate choice. That's led these deeper looks back at his time as Superman and how it went awry.

The current future of DC Universe movies is unclear after major shakeups at DC Studios (following the merger between Skydance and Warner Bros. However, James Gunn still has one last project, his Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow , coming out next year. Actor David Corenswet is fully locked into his role as the DCU Superman, but some fans never give up hope that Henry Cavill will get another chance to suit up and play some alt-universe version (Ultraman) that Corenswet has to face. That's wishful thinking – biut then, we never thought that Black Adam would happen.

You can stream Black Adam and Henry Cavill's other Superman films on HBO Max.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Outer Worlds developer Obsidian Entertainment's upcoming Fallout and the Fallout 3 and New Vegas remasters are seemingly not the only Fallout games in production. According to a classification board rating, there is a new Fallout video game coming out, but it's straying pretty far from the series' RPG roots.

As spotted by the Fallout subreddit , a listing for A Wasteland Full of Cats popped up on October 22nd on the Australian Classification Board , which rates media for the titular island country. It might not immediately seem like a Fallout game based on the title, but the listing itself makes it rather explicit. The description calls it a hidden object game where players find cats inside of a Vault.

"One day there is an accident in the Vault and all of the cats who live there escape out into the Wasteland," reads the description. "It is up to you with the help of some NPCs you meet along the way to find them and return them to the Vault."

This listing notes it will have 14 locations, 33 rooms, and a vault with recognizable elements from the Fallout franchise with puzzles that won't be required for players to hit the credits. Bizarrely, the post also says players will fight radroaches (huge irradiated cockroaches) at the end.

The description ends by saying it is a partnership between developer Devcats and publisher Bethesda. "Zenimax Australia Pty Ltd" is also listed as the party that applied for the rating, further casting aside doubt that this is some AI-generated and legally dubious knock-off.

Unsurprisingly, Devcats is known for its cat-related video games. While some have yet to be released, the studio has developed 17 cat-centric games — 18 counting the Fallout game — on various platforms over the last few years, many of which are only a few bucks and have players clicking around environments to find felines. The "Full of Cats" title is also a pretty consistent naming convention for the team, as nine of its games are part of that series. As such, anyone more interested in this inevitable Fallout-branded installment will likely get a decent peek at what's in store for them by looking at any of those aforementioned nine titles.

A Wasteland Full of Cats has yet to be formally announced by Bethesda or Devcats, thus it is not clear what platforms the game is coming to, how much it will cost, and when it is being released. However, it does seem like it will be announced shortly. Not only do listings on ratings board imply an imminent launch, Devcats also teased on November 12th that it was announcing two more games "soon," likely bringing its total cat games up to 19.

It's a odd collaboration, but it is one that appears to be consistent to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's goals. According to a Bloomberg report, Sharma wants to focus more on the big franchises. A few months later, a Fortune feature noted she even created a new division within Xbox to "centralize and double down on commercial opportunities for top franchises."

This move has come at the cost of many studios and games outside of this focus, as highlighted by Xbox shedding off teams like Double Fine, Arkane Lyon, Ninja Theory, and Undead Labs, all of which mostly worked on lesser-known franchises. But seeing as though many cut developers were working at places like id Software and Halo Studios , it doesn't seem like working on a big franchise makes any developer safe from Xbox's job-cutting hatchet.

Will you play a cat-themed, hidden object game in the Fallout universe? Let us know in the comments.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Since becoming a cultural phenomenon in the early 2000s, the Grand Theft Auto series has been one of the most popular gaming franchises in history. Naturally, this has attracted gamers of all ages looking to play each new entry, despite the fact that the series is clearly geared toward older audiences. With its sandbox open-world and high level of detail, many younger gamers around the globe are undoubtedly trying to convince their parents to let them play Grand Theft Auto 6 this week and be part of the conversation, in spite of its M rating.

If you're finding yourself in this situation within your own family, I can provide more context on just how mature GTA 6 really is, and whether or not you'll want to let a child under the age of 17 play it for themselves. While the ESRB already has a great write-up that explains many of the specifics for why GTA 6 has received a "Mature" rating to begin with, I've completed the game and will help provide additional color to just how much the game pushes the boundaries.

At first glance, the violence in Grand Theft Auto 6 might seem a bit reined in. This isn't like a Mortal Kombat or Gears of War game, where blood and guts are flying everywhere. Instead, GTA 6 is much more rooted in realism, which is reflected in its level of violence. People who are killed quickly fall to the ground, with those who merely get injured being left to writhe on the ground in pain.

While this might seem okay, I actually found the violence in GTA 6 a bit more bothersome at times because of how realistic it seemed. In my opinion, it's easy to write off games like Mortal Kombat that are so over-the-top with their own violence. For GTA 6 to reflect the real world a bit more makes its most brutal moments that much more gruesome.

And just because the gore in GTA 6 isn't as prominent as in other games doesn't mean that it's still not present. Body dismemberment can happen in GTA 6 , although the game does also give you the option to turn this off. Headshots with more powerful weapons can also result in some particularly nasty gore. Given that just about anyone in the world of GTA 6 can be killed at any point, whether by gun, vehicle, or other means, it can lead to the game being particularly brutal.

If you're worried about cursing in Grand Theft Auto 6 , well, there's no way to ignore it. Virtually every swear word you can think of is not only featured in GTA 6 , but they show up incredibly often. By my own estimation, I think I heard the F-bomb alone at least every 30-60 seconds, with certain cutscenes increasing this frequency drastically.

There are also occasional slurs used in GTA 6 as well. These words aren't used flippantly, as they're instead only said by some of the worst people you'll come across in the story of GTA 6 . Still, they're very much present in the game, which is worth keeping in mind.

Crude humor is also prominent throughout Grand Theft Auto 6's world of Leonida. GTA 6's TV channels and radio stations have no filter, with characters being able to say and show anything that they want. As a result, even if you're just driving around and listening to the radio, you never know when you might hear something that's quite vulgar in nature.

Sexual content in Grand Theft Auto 6 is likely where the game pushes things to the limit the most. Strip clubs from the franchise's history are once again present in GTA 6 , which is accompanied by plenty of nudity and raunchy imagery. Engaging with dancers at strip clubs is optional, but there are certain story missions throughout where you'll have to visit these locations no matter what.

Even outside of a sexual context, nudity is also rife throughout GTA 6 . Some of the nudity is played for laughs, but other instances of it, like with the nude beaches you can find, simply have NPCs laying it all bare for the heck of it. Even when characters aren't nude, there are also plenty of others you'll see running around the nude that are scantily clad.

Jason and Lucia, the two main characters in GTA 6 , can also develop a romantic relationship in the game. This leads to instances where players can prompt optional sexual encounters between the two. Not much is ever shown in these moments, as the camera often quickly cuts away, but there's still brief nudity for each shown in the scenes.

Drugs are featured early and often throughout Grand Theft Auto 6 . Not only do both Jason and Lucia smuggle and sell drugs in the game, but they are also given the option to partake in doing certain drugs themselves.

Even if you keep Jason and Lucia clean, there are countless other characters who are not like this. Cocaine is probably the most commonly seen drug throughout the game, but there are other harder drugs mentioned as well. Even though drugs are vital to GTA 6's story and the pursuit of earning money, they're also never glorified in the game, as those who do drugs are often looked down upon.

In short, Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the more mature games I have played in a very, very long time. While many games have received M ratings for much less, GTA 6 feels like it's often pushing the boundaries of this rating.

As someone with kids myself, I can strongly urge that you don't allow them to play Grand Theft Auto 6 until they're older. Although I'm very much opposed to the notion that a game like GTA 6 would turn someone into a criminal themselves, there's still plenty of content within this game that is just not suited for tweens or younger teens. If GTA 6 is anything like its predecessor, it should remain relevant for the better part of the next decade, which means that those who might be too young to play it now should be able to do so at some point once they've aged up a bit.

articles.title: Gordon Ramsay’s Hot Take On Air Fryers Has Me Questioning The Legend
articles.summary: I hate to disagree with the legend on this one, but this feels pretentious.
articles.content:
If there was a Mt. Rushmore for hosts of food television shows, Gordon Ramsay is up there zero questions. As such, I tend to respect the things he says when it comes to the food world, but now I'm questioning the legend. This guy hates air fryers, and I can't help but feel he's being a bit pretentious.

I was willing to defend Ramsay after he dissed pineapple on pizza , as that's a pretty standard opinion to have. I even continue to tune into his shows, despite them largely feeling like the same show as the last one, with a slightly different name .

What I can't abide is the disrespect he showed toward the air fryer. His comments make it sound like it has no place in the standard home kitchen. As someone who cooks from home all the time, I can't praise the air fryer enough, and how it elevates my cooking experience each and every dinner night.

articles.title: Playbill Apologizes Over 'George Floyd Musical' Ad & Bans Producer From Listings; Show's Controversial Creator Previously Sued Off Broadway Venue Over BIPOC Nights
articles.summary: UPDATE, with new Playbill statement: Playbill, the ubiquitous and indispensable New York-based theater publication that features show synopsis, cast biographies and, on its website, stage-related job listings, apologized today for one such ad: a listing calling for singers interested in auditioning for a new concept stage musical album. articles.content:
Playbill , the ubiquitous and indispensable New York-based theater publication that features show synopsis, cast biographies and, on its website, stage-related job listings, apologized today for one such ad: a listing calling for singers interested in auditioning for a new concept stage musical album.

The cast album's title: George Floyd: The Musical .

The so-far-unrecorded and unstaged project carries the tagline, "The $20 Bill That Changed the World!"

The offensive Playbill listing immediately drew comments that were both irate and baffled, including some from Broadway stars. "Wtf," commented Derek Klena. "Ummm….?," wrote Rachel Zegler. And Joy Woods, starring in the current Galileo , surmised the whole thing must be an AI joke. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News Playwrights Horizons Sued Over Discount Tickets For BIPOC Audiences News Broadway's Playbill Joins Twitter Exodus Citing Platform's "Hate, Negativity, And Misinformation"

But it was no joke, at least not the type of joke most on Broadway would appreciate. The company that took out the ad is Busted Broadway , a recently founded New Jersey-based independent musical theater record label developing such projects as Human Centipede: The Musical and Genghis Khan: The Musical (selections from both available on YouTube) and George Floyd: The Musical , coming soon according to the label's website . Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

Floyd was the African American man murdered by a white police officer in Minneapolis, Minnesota, in 2020. Floyd had been identified by a store clerk as having passed a counterfeit $20 bill. One of the police officers who were detaining Floyd at the scene, Derek Chauvin, knelt on the suspect's neck and back, asphyxiating him despite the man's dying plea, "I can't breathe." The killing sparked nationwide protests; Chauvin was found guilty on three murder and manslaughter charges.

This week, outrage over the jobs listing in Playbill was swift. "This is in incredibly poor taste," a commenter wrote. "This isn’t edgy."

And: "Can anyone explain to me why 'George Floyd' and 'comedic Musical' are in the same sentence?? I actually want answers on why this is okay or appropriate???"

And: "I didn’t know systemic racism and violence was comedic." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

And: "Hell isn’t hot enough for yall cause a George Floyd musical, satire or not is in such disgustingly bad taste. For yall it might not matter but he still had a daughter, and a family that have to see yall turn his death into a joke."

And: "Hell is hot & ready for you. Weirdos making an injustice out to be musical. May you never rest."

And then: "Your day is coming."

The reader reaction was enough to push Playbill toward swift, or reasonably swift, action. On its Instagram page today, Playbill wrote: "Late yesterday afternoon, Playbill Jobs incorrectly approved a job listing that had no place on our site. Once leadership was alerted, the listing was immediately removed, and we began reviewing and revising our approval processes. We apologize unequivocally for giving this hateful listing any further air, and we promise to do better going forward. We at Playbill aim to lift up this community with empathy, consideration, and respect. We hope those who read and follow us do the same.

"We know this listing has upset and offended many," Playbill continued, "and the fact that it made it onto our site has disappointed those who trust us as an outlet. For that, we are sorry, and are committed to regaining your trust."

In a just-released statement posted to its social media pages, the record label says, "Busted Broadway seeks to push the limits of what is possible in musical theatre by producing provocative and satirical musical cast albums. Our George Floyd the Musical is NOT making light of, condoning, or mocking the horrific 2020 murder of George Floyd. It's a satire on the CULTURE, rather than the person. Never judge a show by its title, as many who have never seen the script or score appear to be doing now."

Busted Broadway is based in West Milford, New Jersey, and was founded last year, according to its website, "out of a necessity to reinvigorate the barren wasteland of mundane, mediocre musical theatre shows foisted upon audiences today."

The site states that the founders are "a small team of passionate musicians and artists devoted to the funny, absurd, and ridiculous humor baked into our collective human condition." Busted Broadway, the description continues, "is not for the mollycoddled or politically correct listener." The label "exists to shake the snow globe and remind audiences that laughing at dark humor is not only allowed but necessary."

Busted Broadway's mission statement is to create and develop streaming albums and videos "too ridiculous , too raunchy , and too absurd to see the stage…If you like twisted showtunes, dark comedy, and Broadway gone completely off the rails, you’re in the right place."

One of the label's founders and composers is Kevin Lynch , who, according to his bio , is a "Berklee-trained producer, composer, songwriter, and performer [who] has built a career on his tireless momentum—scoring films, directing musical productions, and collaborating with Broadway legends."

"Kevin’s boundless curiosity and innovative approach have established him as a sought-after creative partner, blending experience and intuition with seamless collaboration," the bio states.

Lynch, according to this website , was playing piano by ear at five years old, joined The Juilliard School as staff accompanist, and went on to serve as music director for venues including the Mayo Performing Arts Center, Centenary Stage Company, and Royal Caribbean Cruise Lines.

But until the George Floyd musical, Lynch was perhaps best known for the lawsuit he filed last year against the venerable Off Broadway company Playwrights Horizons condemning the venue's "BIPOC Night," in which patrons who identified as black, indigenous, or people of color were offered discount tickets to a performance of Nazareth Hassan's play Practice . (BIPOC nights had become increasingly common since Broadway's Slave Play used the approach to diversify audiences beyond theater's largely white, largely upper-income attendees.) blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

The lawsuit stated that "because [Lynch] is white, he paid full price. Many other patrons also paid full price for Practice . All are harmed by Playwrights’ discriminatory pricing, and all are entitled to recover."

The suit sought to represent all ticket buyers who allegedly paid more for tickets than the discounted amount. According to the suit, Lynch bought two tickets to Practice for $90 each. Patrons using the BIPOC night discount code paid $39 a ticket.

The suit was settled out of court last May, with Playwrights Horizons releasing a statement saying, “Playwrights Horizons regrets that Mr. Lynch felt excluded because of his race…Playwrights Horizons and Mr. Lynch have agreed to resolve the matter out of court."

In a statement to The New York Times delivered by his attorney after the undisclosed settlement was reached, Lynch indicated he was pleased with the outcome and noted, "Race-based ticket pricing violates all our civil rights, regardless of which race is on the receiving end of the discrimination. I consider it a victory for civil and human rights.”

Deadline has reached out to both Playbill and Busted Broadway for additional comment.

articles.title: One of Storm's Most Disturbing X-Men Stories Is Getting a Horrifying New Chapter in Midnight X-Men
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Midnight X-Men opened its first issue with the mutant vampires already in existence, and it showed that Storm might be the most powerful of them all. The second issue took a break to go back in time and show how this all started, and it looked very familiar. As expected, Storm showed herself to be […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Midnight X-Men opened its first issue with the mutant vampires already in existence, and it showed that Storm might be the most powerful of them all. The second issue took a break to go back in time and show how this all started, and it looked very familiar. As expected, Storm showed herself to be a powerful and very well-respected empyre, and the second issue showed that she was also where it all began. This book showed the origin story of the mutants becoming vampires, and Storm was the first of them all after Dracula convinced her to change and accept his invitation to turn willingly.

In Midnight X-Men #2 by Jonathan Hickman and Matteo Della Fonte, Dracula tempted Storm to change, and she accepted. Storm then set a trap to lure in the X-Men and helped Dracula change them all in the ultimate betrayal. This played into the first time that Storm met Dracula, and in that previous meeting, Storm refused his temptations.

Midnight X-Men #2 showed how this terrible timeline ended up creating a war between vampires, empyres, mutants, and humans. This all started when Dracula summoned Storm to him. He then explained his entire origin to her, including how his own master took his life when his master realized the weakness of seeing his own kind being hunted down and killed. However, in Storm, he saw that she was different, calling her the most powerful and mighty of all the mutants. He offered to give her eternity, and she agreed and gave herself over to him.

That led Storm to become the first empyre, and then she did the unthinkable. She called out for help, pulled in the X-Men, attacked them with Dracula, and turned them too. Dracula and Storm turned Iceman, Angel, Beast, and Jean Grey. Only Cyclops and Kitty Pryde escaped. After this, Jean Grey tricked Cyclops into returning with a new team to save her, and it was another trap, with Storm once again showing her place as the leader. By the end, Storm and her new empyres had turned or killed several mutants, and she was a genuine villain. While she seemed almost sympathetic when meeting with Nightcrawler in the first issue, she was corrupted here.

This calls back to a previous X-Men issue, the first time that Storm met Dracula. In The Uncanny X-Men #159 (1982), Storm was out walking alone in New York City when she was attacked by someone. She began to grow weak, and it was Kitty Pryde who realized that something was wrong with her and that it might tie into the legend of vampires. When Storm disappeared, Kitty Pryde told the X-Men that she believed Dracula was responsible, and the mutants learned it was true.

This led the X-Men to seek her out at Belvedere Castle, and they soon realized they couldn't match up to the legendary vampire. However, the setup here was hugely different from what happened in Midnight X-Men . The setup was different. In Midnight X-Men , Dracula lured Storm in and gave her the choice, although that is not to say that he wasn't using some of his vampire powers of hypnosis on the mutant. In this earlier story, he fed on her and tried to force her to become one of his brides against her will.

That was the main difference. When Kitty Pryde gave herself to Storm and said she was willing to die, that snapped Storm out of it. Dracula told Storm to slaughter her teammates in the X-Men, and she attacked Dracula instead. This led to a giant battle between her and Dracula, which ended with Dracula finally admitting he admired her standing up for herself, then leaving, while also declaring that they were enemies forever. It was a wild and different X-Men story for the time, and it clearly influenced the new Midnight X-Men comic series.

That story was also carried over to Mutant X by Howard Mackie and Tom Raney in 1998. That series was another multiversal story, this one with Havok ending up on a different Earth where Storm couldn't stop the transformation but remained a hero. She eventually killed Dracula in this timeline, and she kept working as a hero on a team called the Six, which showed that even as a vampire, Storm could be a hero. Midnight X-Men , though, showed the worst-case scenario, where Storm turned her own kind and helped slaughter those mutants not deemed worthy. This was a nightmare scenario of that classic X-Men storyline.

What are your thoughts on Midnight X-Men and making Storm its catalyst? Let us know how you think this storyline will end up in the comments below.

Seriously, if you’re a movie fan, it’s one of the best places to see a ton of classics.

articles.title: Judge Allows Trump to Sue New York Times Reporters Over Tax Fraud Claims
articles.summary: A judge has allowed President Trump to proceed with a $15 billion suit against the New York Times, finding a plausible claim that its reporters acted recklessly in accusing Trump of tax fraud. Judge Steven Merryday denied the defendants' motion to dismiss the lawsuit, holding that the book "Lucky Loser" includes a series of claims […]
articles.content:
A judge has allowed President Trump to proceed with a $15 billion suit against the New York Times , finding a plausible claim that its reporters acted recklessly in accusing Trump of tax fraud.

Judge Steven Merryday denied the defendants' motion to dismiss the lawsuit, holding that the book "Lucky Loser" includes a series of claims about Trump's business dealings that are potentially defamatory. Related Stories Chris Pratt to Star in Sci-Fi Family Drama 'The Traveler,' Inks First-Look Producing Deal at Paramount (EXCLUSIVE) Chris Pratt to Continue 'Terminal List' Story in 'Savage Son' Series for Amazon

Though the book cites tax experts who stated that Trump's conduct was "highly suspicious" and "smells like a crime," the judge ruled that was not enough to state outright that Trump had committed tax fraud or tax evasion. Such a clear-cut judgment would require "an explicit opinion from a qualified source after a thorough examination of pertinent facts," the judge ruled. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Absent such a statement, the judge ruled that the reporters were venturing into risky territory.

"They know that they don’t know, but they are undeterred," he wrote.

The book, published by Penguin Random House, included the allegation that Trump had obtained the equivalent of $400 million from his father, Fred, "much of it through fraudulent tax evasion schemes." The book also asserted that Fred Trump had engaged in "likely tax fraud" when he gave his son gifts disguised as loans; and that the arrangement was designed to avoid gift and estate taxes.

In his lawsuit , Trump argued that the statements were false because neither he nor his father had ever been charged with a tax crime.

The New York Times published two articles drawn from the book in 2024. In the ruling, Merryday dismissed the claims pertaining to the first article, which focused on Trump's relationship with TV producer Mark Burnett and the development of "The Apprentice." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The judge also tossed statements from the second article that focused on Trump's school record. But the judge allowed Trump to sue over a statement from that article that authorities had investigated his "ties to the Mafia" and had found "violations of money laundering laws."

The same judge dismissed an earlier version of Trump's lawsuit last year, finding it overlong and full of colorful but irrelevant detail. Trump's lawyers refiled a more concise version a month later.

The suit can now proceed to discovery and motions for summary judgment. The defendants in the case are the Times, three of its reporters, and Penguin Random House.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A new Star Wars Jedi 3 report has surfaced online, giving a new update on the confirmed but unrevealed Star Wars game. The new report comes from Nash Weedle, a source primarily known for information pertaining to Nintendo and Nintendo games, but who occasionally branches out beyond the realm of Nintendo. According to the insider, Star Wars Jedi 3 is poised to be announced soon.

Adding to this, Nash Weedle relays word that a reveal at The Game Awards in December could happen. And this wouldn't be surprising considering the series' history. As fans will know, Star Wars Jedi Survivor's release date was announced at The Game Awards alongside the reveal of its gameplay. So, there is precedent with the series and The Game Awards. That said, Nash Weedle also notes that it's possible the announcement is going to be saved for Star Wars' 50th anniversary.

In addition to this, the insider leaks that the first two games — Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order and Star Wars Jedi: Survivor — are both coming to Nintendo Switch 2. There is no word on when these releases will happen, but it would presumably be before the third game arrives, if the new game is going to launch on Switch 2. If it's going to come to Switch 2 after launch, then so will these ports, most likely.

Of course, take all of this new information with a grain of salt. None of this is official information, and even if it is accurate, it is subject to change that could render it inaccurate. So far, it has not drawn out the series developer, Respawn Entertainment, nor its publisher, EA. The latter owns the former, for those who do not know, so most communications for the former come through the latter. For a variety of reasons, we do not expect either to budge on their positions of silence and comment, but if either does, we will update the story accordingly.

Recent reports about Star Wars Jedi 3 have suggested its release date is close , which in turn means its reveal would have to be close. To this end, there is scuttlebutt that the game is planning to release in the holiday season of 2027. If this is the case, then it will almost certainly be revealed before the end of the year, or the first 3-4 months of the new year.

Officially, the game has been confirmed to be in development; we just don't have the following salient details: when it's going to be revealed, when it's going to be released, and what platforms it will release on. And, of course, we do not have any details on what the game will be about.

In fact, just getting through the show can be such a hectic ordeal for the host that they’re assigned someone to manage their schedule, keep them fed and make sure they’re in the right place and wearing the right costume at the right time. It turns out it’s the same employee every week. Her name is Donna Richards, and she’s apparently seen all the famous people naked.

During a recent episode of Good Hang with Amy Poehler , Richards and her role on the show came up after guest Jack Black talked about her hunting down an Italian chopped salad for him because he was starving between dress rehearsal and the live show. Apparently she’s there to make sure the host is relaxed, comfortable and dressed to perform. Sometimes that means making sure they’ve eaten, and sometimes that means physically yanking clothes on and off them during frantic costume changes between sketches . Here’s a portion of what Poehler said…

She has this really specific job that’s like part nurse, part coach where she kinda grabs you and dresses you from scene to scene. She has your whole show in her hand. She makes sure you can do it. She is the one that if you pass out or you forgot something and turn to her and say I don’t remember, she would have you. She’s your wrangler. She’s seen everybody naked. She’s seen every star naked.

SNL fans are very familiar with the work it takes to pitch, write and rehearse the show every week , but there’s a lot less familiarity around the actual mechanics of making the live show happen. It’s ultimately because of people like Richards and other unsung heroes who make sure their more famous co-workers are physically able to go out there and make us laugh. It’s better for everyone if Jack Black is worried about being funny and not worried about remembering which outfit he’s supposed to get into next and which wig it pairs with.

During the same conversation, Poehler said Richards could write a great book just recounting all of the ridiculous requests that she’s gotten since she started on the show. Apparently, Black asking for an Italian chopped salad without onions is incredibly tame compared to the nonsense she’s normally asked to do, but fortunately, she’s been able to weather those storms and build amazing relationships with cast members and many of the celebrities who have hosted.

Tina Fey made sure she got her moment to appear on camera during SNL ’s 50th Anniversary , and she’s been the subject of a bunch of fun interviews like this where cast members and celebrities shout her out. She’s even apparently developed a fun little bond with Jason Momoa who has come and visited her on a few different occasions.

articles.title: The Cliff Booth Reviews Point Out A Missed Opportunity In Brad Pitt’s Sequel, And I Have To Agree
articles.summary: What's it like to hang out with Cliff Booth without Rick Dalton?
articles.content:
I had the chance to see The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth at its glitzy Los Angeles premiere earlier this week, and I must say, I think fans of Once Upon A Time… In Hollywood are in for a treat. The sequel comes from an original script by Quentin Tarantino , and stars Brad Pitt under the direction of Se7en and Fight Club ’s David Fincher . Talk about a dream trio! The reviews just dropped for the 1977-set flick, and a lot of people are bringing up something that could have been that I thought about myself.

One massive pro of it being a movie is that film buffs can experience the crime-comedy on IMAX screens next week, ahead of it being available to stream with a Netflix subscription in December. I very much enjoyed watching it in theaters, especially for all the audience reactions. I should also point out the film very much has the three-act structure of a movie, and doesn’t feel unfinished. However, it definitely feels like there’s a bigger world Tarantino has created that the film didn't have time to fully get to. Check out what The Hollywood Reporter ’s David Rooney said on the subject:

Cliff Booth has an incredible cast that features some especially memorable parts for Elizabeth Debicki, as a talent agent and the object of Cliff’s affections, and Scott Caan, who plays a popular TV star who needs Cliff’s particular set of skills. But then there are characters like Yahya Abdul-Mateen II ’s Roderick "Hot Rod" Harrison and Carla Gugino’s Toni Peters, who feel less meaty than they could have been. Here’s what IndieWire’s David Ehrich said about the movie, which he also called a “disappointing compromise between great directors”:

Outside of the conversation around how making Cliff Booth into a movie might have been a missed opportunity, there’s a lot of glowing praise for the film. Screen Daily ’s Tim Grierson was particularly impressed by the mashup between filmmakers, writing:

Then there’s a four-star review from The Guardian ’s Peter Bradshaw. The critic called Pitt’s performance “endlessly watchable and entertaining, but also enigmatic,” along with noting these thoughts about the filmmaking:

articles.title: What's Taking the BioShock Movie So Long? Director Reveals It's the Same Problem Other Video Games Have
articles.summary: BioShock's shift from video game to big-screen movie is something that's been talked about for years now, and it clearly hasn't been easy. Attempts have been made since the game first released back in 2008 to bring it to life, with filmmakers like Gore Verbinski attached at one point and even Oscar-winner Guillermo del Toro […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google BioShock 's shift from video game to big-screen movie is something that's been talked about for years now , and it clearly hasn't been easy. Attempts have been made since the game first released back in 2008 to bring it to life, with filmmakers like Gore Verbinski attached at one point and even Oscar-winner Guillermo del Toro giving it the old college try . Despite almost two decades of trying, though, nothing has been made. Netflix has been attempting to get their own version of the ground for a few years with The Hunger Games franchise director Francis Lawrence attached, and the filmmaker has finally admitted they have a problem.

Speaking with Empire , Lawrence reiterated that the BioShock film is still being worked out and they're "trying to crack it" but this is hardly an update on the film's status at all . That said, Lawrence did reveal what the hold-up is in figuring out how to make it work, confirming that like almost every other video game movie, creating a main character for the story is proving to be its biggest challenge. “That's been the trick: creating the character almost out of whole cloth,” Lawrence added. “Who this person is – what is their emotional journey?”

As fans who played the game will recall, the original BioShock put players in the shoes of Jack, a faceless protagonist that was something of a cypher for the larger machinations of Andrew Ryan and his underwater city of Rapture . Eventually his backstory is revealed, confirming his actual connections to what's going on in the plot, but for the most part the game relies on player choice to determine its ending and allows you to fill in the gaps of what kind of person Jack really is.

That in mind, it's easy to see why turning Jack into a relatable protagonist with his own storyline (before all the twists and turns) is something that would be tough to figure out for the movie. On top of it all, making the protagonist himself relatable and worth spending two hours with has to come on top of recreating a distinct world with unique lore, wild monsters, and even the superpowers that he unlocks for himself along the way.

“I think one of the biggest challenges is that we really want to honour the spirit of the game, its themes, the mythology of the world, and the people who inhabit it," Lawrence added, indicating that the conversations every BioShock fan has had about bringing the game to life is one they've already engaged with.

As gamers know well, though, creating a wholly relatable movie character out of a video game protagonist has been a problem for adaptations for the past thirty years. It's one reason why the stigma of video game movies managed to stick around as long as it did, on top of having to create a whole narrative on top of something that didn't actually have one. That said, BioShock has done a lot of the heavy lifting for the movie in terms of the larger plot and the look of the world, and it would have been easy to fart out a movie that just replicated its visual aesthetic and had no real character at the center. Knowing they don't want to make something that easy is a good sign.

articles.title: 'GTA 6' Sales Have Already Surpassed Christopher Nolan's 'The Odyssey'
articles.summary: The Rockstar Games epic has generated $1.84 billion in sales — and it just launched today.
articles.content:
For those wondering why Rockstar Games hasn't licensed Grand Theft Auto for a movie or TV show, this is probably why.

Grand Theft Auto VI has already generated an incredible $1.84 billion in sales, according to market intelligence firm Sensor Tower .

The GTA 6 's eye-popping sales figure may already be outdated. articles.title: Sequels, Subtitles and Spring Releases: How the Best Picture Race Is Rewriting the Academy’s Playbook
articles.summary: Somebody at every awards season party, and everybody on the internet, will tell you why a movie can’t grab a best picture nomination — or even win the prize. It opened too early. It’s a sequel. It has subtitles. It made no money. It’s a documentary. And then the Academy goes and proves everyone wrong. […]
articles.content:
Somebody at every awards season party, and everybody on the internet, will tell you why a movie can’t grab a best picture nomination — or even win the prize. It opened too early. It’s a sequel. It has subtitles. It made no money. It’s a documentary.

And then the Academy goes and proves everyone wrong.

With the fall festivals in the rearview mirror and the holiday corridor still loading, it’s time to take a look at the best picture race. Christopher Nolan’s “ The Odyssey ” holds the top spot on Variety’s best picture chart and nearly every pundit’s list. But the margin between No. 1 and No. 20 feels thinner than it has in years. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories China Box Office: 'Resident Evil' Holds Top Spot for Fourth Straight Frame as 2014's 'John Wick' Debuts in Third

A24 has many films in the projected lineup. Warner Bros., the reigning champion after its “One Battle After Another” win, with a new boss at the helm of the company, Skydance CEO David Ellison, is keeping Denis Villeneuve’s franchise finale, “ Dune: Part Three ,” close to the vest until December.

And we’re still waiting for Robert Eggers’ “Werwulf,” with Aaron Taylor-Johnson. That film could shake up the race once voters finally get a look at it, and, for argument’s sake, so can “Avengers: Doomsday” from the Russo brothers.

That leaves 20 to 30 films chasing 10 slots, each making its strongest case for why it belongs. Standing in the way are the old rules, and this season is poised to test every one of them.

SUMMER BLOCKBUSTERS FADE BY THE WINTER

Nolan has already broken this rule himself. Universal Pictures’ “Oppenheimer” opened in July 2023 and won seven Oscars the following March. Three years later, “The Odyssey,” the adaptation of Homer’s Greek epic, has the footprint that can lead the nominations field, with an eye on the record 16 nominations “Sinners” set last season. As Odysseus, Matt Damon anchors the voyage home; co-stars Anne Hathaway and Samantha Morton are both tracking for supporting actress recognition, while John Leguizamo and Robert Pattinson are legitimate supporting actor threats. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The bigger question is whether five months of fresher challengers will wear it down.

SEQUELS HAVE DIFFICULTY WINNING

That’s because only two have. “The Godfather Part II” (1974) followed the 1973 best picture winner, “The Godfather,” and “The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King” (2003) remains the only sequel to win after its earlier chapters fell short. The latter provides the playbook for Warner Bros.’ “Dune: Part Three,” which arrives after Villeneuve was left out of the directing lineup for both previous installments. Almost nobody has seen the finale, but Zendaya’s expanded role gives it an acting hook the earlier chapters lacked.

Further down the list, Netflix’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” tests the same rule, with David Fincher directing a Quentin Tarantino script based on his 2019 hit “Once Upon a Time … in Hollywood.”

SUBTITLES AND STREAMERS MUST CLEAR HURDLES

Bong Joon Ho’s “Parasite” remains the only non-English-language film to win best picture. Netflix is still waiting for its first, after coming painfully close with “Roma” (2018) and “Emilia Pérez” (2024). Enter the Cannes sensation “La Bola Negra,” the streamer’s Spanish-language drama from Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi. It has Penélope Cruz in the supporting actress conversation, singer-turned-actor Guitarricadelafuente emerging as one of the season’s breakout performers and an international feature campaign supported by a passionate base. It has the texture of a film that could finally get Netflix a win.

Neon won with “Parasite” and “Anora,” both Palme d’Or winners, and it has this year’s Palme winner, too: Cristian Mungiu’s drama “Fjord,” starring Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve. But its slot is not a sure thing in the best picture race with any number of international contenders waiting for a late surge, including Lee Chang-dong’s “Possible Love” from South Korea, Andrey Zvyagintsev’s “Minotaur” from Mubi and Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s “All of a Sudden,” also from Neon.

COMEDIES DON’T GET TAKEN SERIOUSLY blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Then again, not all of these comedies are funny. Martin McDonagh is back for another round with “Wild Horse Nine,” following “The Banshees of Inisherin” (2022), which went home empty-handed despite nine nominations. John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell deliver the kind of performances that could get the actors’ branch buzzing.

A24 is doubling down on laughs. “The Invite” has director and star Olivia Wilde vying for at least two nominations, along with her ensemble. Jesse Eisenberg’s “The Debut” features best actress front-runner Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti, who is tracking for his third Oscar nom and possible first win. The indie label also has “Club Kid,” from debut director Jordan Firstman, looking for awards season love after declaring itself a drama for the Golden Globes.

Meanwhile, Mike Leigh’s “Tender Loving Care,” from Bleecker Street, is entering the Golden Globes race as a comedy, but is more likely to leave audiences in tears than have them laughing.

DOCUMENTARIES AND CARTOONS ARE SPILLING OUT OF THEIR OWN CATEGORIES

No documentary has ever been nominated for best picture, and three animated films have, with none winning. A24’s “You Can See Everything,” from Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, looks more like a sure thing by the day after winning over audiences at industry screenings. It doesn’t hurt that it has become one of the biggest-grossing documentaries in decades.

Laika’s stop-motion epic “Wildwood” is the rare animated feature with a credible best picture argument. Voters have shown they’ll go there when the craft is undeniable.

SPRING RELEASES CAN BE FORGOTTEN

“Everything Everywhere All at Once” opened in March and swept the Oscars the following year. Amazon MGM’s “Project Hail Mary” opened in March, too, and Phil Lord and Christopher Miller’s adaptation of Andy Weir’s novel is the crowd-pleaser of this race. Crowd-pleasers can survive the preferential ballot, especially with Ryan Gosling firmly in the best actor conversation. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Antoine Fuqua’s “Michael,” from Lionsgate, opened in April and became the highest-grossing biopic of all time. Jaafar Jackson hopes to crack the best actor race for playing his uncle, Michael Jackson, while Colman Domingo’s turn as patriarch Joe Jackson is in the supporting actor conversation.

ONE PERFORMANCE CAN CARRY A PICTURE

Don’t tell the actors’ branch. It’s the Academy’s largest, and it has a way of carrying its favorites across the categories. Neon’s “Artificial” has the supporting actor front-runner in Andrew Garfield’s portrayal of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Focus Features acquired “Elsinore” over the summer and hopes Andrew Scott’s towering performance as Ian Charleson can carry it into the best picture race.

Pedro Pascal in Tony Gilroy’s “Behemoth!” and Inde Navarrette in the horror breakout “Obsession” are among the likeliest performers to pull their films into other categories. The same goes for newcomer Anthony Ippolito, so authentic as Sylvester Stallone in Peter Farrelly’s “I Play Rocky” — it’s the kind of underdog story voters love. John Turturro’s performance in “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York” from Sony Pictures Classics is also in the best actor conversation.

A few others are flying under the radar but still looking for a defining moment this season. Sumerian Pictures’ “Josephine” won the Grand Jury Prize at Sundance, while Apple’s “Being Heumann” finished as the second runner-up for the People’s Choice Award at TIFF.

The lesson of the past few seasons is that the race is never settled in November. It just looks that way.

articles.title: Marvel's Incredible Hulk Got the Worst Kind of TV Ending, But Returned Like No One Expected
articles.summary: TV tends to be less than generous when it comes to wrapping up superhero stories. Sometimes the show we love gets a proper send-off, a satisfying ending, and the hero gets to do one last rescue. Other times, the network simply pulls the plug and leaves everybody wondering what happened next. Bill Bixby's The Incredible […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google TV tends to be less than generous when it comes to wrapping up superhero stories. Sometimes the show we love gets a proper send-off, a satisfying ending, and the hero gets to do one last rescue. Other times, the network simply pulls the plug and leaves everybody wondering what happened next. Bill Bixby's The Incredible Hulk got the second treatment, which is especially unfortunate when you consider how much viewers had invested in David Banner's seemingly endless search for a cure.

In a twist of irony, the Hulk story did not end on television. After CBS pulled the plug on the weekly series, Banner and his oversized green other half re-emerged, not in a series wrap-up, but in a string of made-for-television movies that took the story in astonishingly different directions. He even managed to bring us a few familiar comic book heroes while he was at it. While some may have considered the closure of the original series odd, the way in which this television comeback was played out is perhaps even more astonishing. And if you're a Hulk fan, you'll want to check out the equally great Hulk cartoon series that was surprisingly accurate to the Marvel Comics series.

The Incredible Hulk debuted in 1977 with a bit of a twist on the typical superhero fare viewers might have been anticipating. Bill Bixby portrayed David Banner as a conflicted scientist on the run, a character who drove from town to town in desperate search of a cure. When he lost control to rage or stress, it was Lou Ferrigno who appeared as the big green Hulk. When reporter Jack McGee, played by Jack Colvin, kept hounding the elusive beast across the country, Banner had yet another reason to keep running. The series ran for five seasons on CBS and developed a loyal following. Yet its eventual departure didn't give viewers the kind of finale that usually comes with a long-running television adventure. CBS decided the series had run its course, and the cancellation left Banner's story hanging.

For me, the show's introduction was absolutely incredible. If you've never seen it, do yourself a favor and check it out. The lack of CGI also added an incredible sense of realism, and it genuinely frightened me when I first watched it as a wee little lad. Even today, I can appreciate the practical production techniques the show used, and it remains one of my favorite Marvel TV shows—even more so than many of Disney's current iterations.

The last episode, "A Minor Problem," has an almost overly subtle title, considering that it is the final episode of the regular series. Banner arrives in a town dealing with an E. coli outbreak and does his best to support the victims. By the end of the episode he is back on the road and back in search of a cure; the episode features neither the big showdown with McGee, any further advancement of Banner's research, nor any resolution for the character. It wasn’t meant as a series finale, but it would be the last episode CBS would air. Johnson, the series creator, had a concept for a finale that would have given Banner a way out of the transformations, but CBS declined it. When your premise involves a man's search for a cure, a series finale with Banner going nowhere quickly becomes a rather unsatisfactory end.

However, the story of Banner was not finished with those events; television would assist in the next chapter. In 1988, Bill Bixby and Lou Ferrigno returned for The Incredible Hulk Returns , a made-for-TV movie that brought the characters back to NBC. This time, Banner wasn't just dealing with his familiar green problem. He also encountered Donald Blake and his rather unusual connection to Thor. Played by Eric Allan Kramer, the Norse god brought a whole new superhero into the world of Bixby's television series. It was a pretty remarkable development for viewers who had spent years watching Banner travel from town to town. Suddenly, the show had another Marvel hero running around, complete with a magical hammer and an entirely different mythology. The movie even served as a potential launching point for a Thor television series, although that never happened. Apparently, one superhero wasn't quite enough for Banner's comeback.

Marvel wasn't finished experimenting with the format, either. The following year brought The Trial of the Incredible Hulk , which introduced Rex Smith as Matt Murdock and his masked identity as Daredevil. John Rhys-Davies also appeared as Wilson Fisk, better known as the Kingpin. That's quite a collection of Marvel characters for a television movie that began with David Banner trying to get his life back together. Bixby directed the film himself and continued to expand the world of the original series. Then came The Death of the Incredible Hulk in 1990, which finally gave Banner's long journey a definitive ending. The title doesn't leave much room for interpretation, and the film takes the character somewhere considerably darker than his usual adventures. It wasn't necessarily the conclusion every fan wanted, but at least Banner finally got an ending that the original television series never had the opportunity to provide. After being left wandering the country by CBS, the Hulk had managed to return for three more adventures and even share the screen with some of Marvel's biggest heroes.
