articles.summary: Netflix is continuing to mine content from some of the most acclaimed cult-hit properties of the 1980s, 1990s and 2000s. After turning The Witcher and The Sandman into acclaimed hits, Netflix is taking on Grendel, the comic book series that author Matt Wagner first launched in 1982. Grendel has been an unusual icon in comics: […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Netflix is continuing to mine content from some of the most acclaimed cult-hit properties of the 1980s, 1990s and 2000s. After turning The Witcher and The Sandman into acclaimed hits, Netflix is taking on Grendel , the comic book series that author Matt Wagner first launched in 1982. Grendel has been an unusual icon in comics: the publishing rights have taken several sharp turns, while the sporadic nature of the character's books and lore is a puzzle not every fan has put together. So what is Netflix doing now that so many other failed adaptations couldn't?

Grendel will be adapted as an animated series by studio Bobbypills, which produces DC's Creature Commandos , with Bobak Esfarjani ( Alien: Earth, Widow's Bay ) acting as showrunner, writer, and executive producer. Now Netflix is releasing full details on the series and who is invovled, which you can read below.

“ Grendel has been at the forefront of independent comics for over forty years, and we’re thrilled to bring Matt Wagner’s creation to Netflix,” John Derderian, Vice President, Animation Series + Kids & Family TV at Netflix, said in a statement. “Like the comic, this animated series will break the traditional superhero mold just as Matt's time-honored comic book has always done. Bobak, Dark Horse Entertainment and Bobbypills are bold storytellers who love this world as much as its fans do, and we’re so excited to partner with them to bring this story to screen.”

Dark Horse Comics was the publisher that picked up Grendel and relaunched it in 1992 after the comic's original publisher, Comico, went bankrupt at the end of the '80s. Chris Tongue, Tim Wiesch, and Jay Komas of Dark Horse Entertainment will be attached as executive producers, alongside Matt Wagner and Lydia Antonini.

"It’s incredibly exciting to see my creation finally make this leap to the animated screen!" Matt Wagner wrote in his statment. "Netflix’s dynamic new series retains the source material’s dark adult themes and also brings a fresh and thrilling approach to the narrative. This is Grendel as I’ve always wanted to see the character portrayed—a hyper-kinetic level of action, bracing explosions of violence and a poignant engaging storyline.”

Grendel has followed several characters who have taken up the titular mantle and been tragically influenced by it. It started with Hunter Rose, an author who moonlights as a masked assassin and eventually becomes the head of New York City's organized crime world.

The Netflix series follows the framework of the original character and story. As per the show's logline: "After the woman he loves is shockingly murdered, Hunter Rose devotes himself to one thing: vengeance. But as he tears through street gangs, the elite, and New York City’s supernatural underworld in pursuit of her killer, a chance at a real life forces him to choose: walk away from ultimate power, or become the very monster he hunts."

Grendel is in development at Netflix. No release date has been set yet.

articles.content:
If your idea of an awesome movie-watching experience involves strapping a VR headset to your head, Meta has got you.

On Thursday, Meta announced that it has launched over 150 3D movies available to rent or purchase in the TV app for Meta Quest 3 and 3S virtual-reality headsets. Initially, the feature is available only in the U.S.

Movies available for Meta Quest users include James Cameron's "Avatar," "Spider-Man: Far From Home," "Jurassic World Rebirth," "Wicked: For Good," and Billie Eilish's "Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour." Co-directed by Eilish and Cameron, the concert film will be exclusively available to buy and rent in 3D through Dec. 31 on Meta Quest. The tech company has deals in the works for more movies: Meta said the TV app's library will expand to "thousands of titles," along international availability, with the launch of Meta VR Glasses in spring 2027 , to cost $1,299 apiece.

Quest VR users have already been able to stream movies and TV shows using native apps for services including YouTube, Amazon Prime Video and Disney+ (which offers select movies in 3D) or access streaming services like Netflix or Apple TV using the built-in browser.

Meta continues to push the VR headset as a premium home-theater experience. With the latest Meta Quest software update, the devices' "Theater" mode provides a big screen and dims viewers' surroundings for a personal cinema experience.

Watching "Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour" in 3D on Meta Quest, "you can stand alongside Billie, look out at the crowd, and feel like part of the show," according to Meta. "Getting those shots took more than pointing cameras at a stage. Billie performs on a 360-degree stage surrounded by the audience, so Cameron's Lightstorm Vision team built a new system for filming 3D at long range, capturing the action up close without putting cameras between Billie and her fans. Another 3D camera on stage puts you right beside her."

EXCLUSIVE : National Geographic is exploring the people and decisions behind pivotal events of the past three decades with its latest documentary slate.

The Disney-owned brand has greenlit three documentaries about the brother of the Unabomber, Somali pirates and the Hantavirus.

My Brother The Unabomber , Hantavirus: The Inside Story and Hijacked: The Real Captain Phillips will all premiere on Disney+, Hulu and Nat Geo .

“These are names and events everyone recognizes,” said Tom McDonald, EVP, National Geographic Content. “But behind each name is an extraordinary story. My Brother The Unabomber comes from David Abraham’s Wonderhood Studios. It tells the the story of a man faced with the impossible choice of turning in his own brother during the final year of the Unabomber manhunt. It features access to David Kaczynski, the brother of Unabomber Ted Kaczynski and previously unseen archive, including letters between the brothers and explores the decision that he and his wife Linda faced when they read his manifesto in the papers before reporting their suspicions to the FBI. Hijacked: The Real Captain Phillips comes from Curious Films. The three-part series revisits the 2009 hijacking of the Maersk Alabama, when Somali pirates seized the American cargo ship, and the military rescue operation that followed. It brings together the experiences of Captain Richard Phillips and his crew with the rarely heard stories of the Somali pirates at the heart of the hijacking, and explores who the Somali men were, the circumstances in Somalia that drove them to sea, and how events unfolded from their point of view. It also features never-before-seen archive, including U.S. Navy footage.

Christian Collerton is series director, Dov Freedman, Jessie Versluys and Jamal Osman exec produce for Curious Films and Carolyn Payne exec produces for Nat Geo.
